title: Lucious Selmon: Sooner Star Turned Longtime Coach
question: What did Lucious Selmon do after playing football at Oklahoma?
answer: After his unanimous All-America season in 1973, Lucious Selmon returned to Oklahoma as an assistant coach for 19 seasons (1976-1994), then coached for the NFL's Jacksonville Jaguars from 1995 to 2002. He was named to the SEC Football Legends class of 2025.
summary: Lucious Selmon, the oldest Selmon brother, went from OU All-American to 19 years on the Sooners staff, eight with the Jaguars, and an SEC Legends honor.
body: Fans know the Selmon name for Lee Roy and Dewey, but the oldest of the three brothers, Lucious, blazed the trail. Born in Muskogee and raised near Eufaula, he came to Norman first, and his younger brothers followed him to Oklahoma.

On the field, Lucious was a defensive lineman who started 31 of 35 games for the Sooners from 1971 through 1973. Oklahoma went 32-2-1 in those three seasons and won Big Eight titles in 1972 and 1973. As a senior in 1973 he was a unanimous first-team All-American and was named the Big Eight's defensive player of the year. That fall, all three Selmon brothers were on the same OU roster.

Football did not end for him after the final whistle. Lucious joined the Oklahoma coaching staff in 1976 and stayed for 19 seasons, through 1994. During that stretch the Sooners claimed nine Big Eight titles and the 1985 national championship.
In 1995 he moved to the NFL as an assistant with the Jacksonville Jaguars, a job that lasted through the 2002 season. He later worked on the Michigan State staff as well.

In 2025 the Southeastern Conference named him to its Football Legends class, which honors former players and coaches from its member schools. He became the second Oklahoma representative since the Sooners joined the SEC, following Barry Switzer in 2024.
